SMTO-GML-0008 — SMTO must show you which emails it will change first

GUID: bab1361f-1cb8-4018-b14e-a115033a310b
Slug: gmail-bulk-preview-required
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO tried to change a group of emails picked by a search without first showing you exactly which emails those are. It stopped, and no emails were changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO again, for example "Show me which emails will be archived, then archive them." SMTO needs a fresh list of the exact emails before it can change many at once.
  2. Check the number of emails and the examples SMTO shows. If they look wrong, change your search words first. Your mailbox may have changed, so the list could differ from what you expect.
  3. When SMTO asks for approval, approve only if the list matches what you want changed. Your approval locks in that exact set of emails.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports how many emails it changed, and they show the change in Gmail.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't approve a change for a list you haven't seen.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • gmail.batch_modify was called with a query or label selector, or without explicit message IDs, and no selection_token from gmail.preview_modify, so the bulk change was refused before any mailbox write.

What this means

  • Batch mutation has no selection_token while it uses a query/label selector or lacks explicit message IDs. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Batch mutation has no selection_token while it uses a query/label selector or lacks explicit message IDs.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect whether the request uses explicit IDs or a query-based selection requiring a token.

How to fix it

  • Call gmail.preview_modify with the same account, operation, label and query, have the user approve that exact selection, then pass its selection_token to gmail.batch_modify (or use a named action such as gmail.mark_all_read, which previews and approves internally). Do not reuse an old token or ID list after the mailbox changed.
  • Generate a fresh preview and explicitly confirm the exact intended selection.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A fresh exact preview is confirmed and submitted through the supported bulk flow.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
